Trust decision: a per-key denylist (`isSafeUrlSegmentBase` + strict-lang / loose-ns helpers, consulted by `interpolateUrl`) decides whether `lng`/`ns` may be interpolated into a loadPath/addPath template; at the pinned commit it omits `:` and ns `//`, so a placeholder-leading template becomes an absolute/protocol-relative URL.
`pattern_fit`: A — the published fix spans `lib/utils.js` plus a checked-in CDN bundle (`i18nextHttpBackend.js`/`.min.js`) that no test imports.
Strongest lever: coupled behaviour — ns must reject `//` while keeping `a/b` and `@org/pkg` (3.0.6/4.0.1 exceptions), so an over-broad `/` or `@` ban breaks documented legitimate behaviour.
Biggest red flag: `tiny_repo` (three-file `lib/`, ~300 lines; the whole protection is readable in one pass).
